l1: What activation method is expected — KMS, MAK, Active Directory-based, or subscription (E3/E5)?
What is the exact activation error code shown in Settings or from slmgr /dlv?
Is this a single device or a broader fleet activation failure?
Was this device recently re-imaged, migrated, or hardware-changed?
How many machines are affected, and did they all start failing around the same date and time?
Was the problematic machine successfully activated before, and if so, when did the issue start?
Is the customer able to reproduce the activation failure consistently, or does it resolve itself after a retry or reboot?
l2: Is the KMS host reachable and reporting a current count at or above the minimum threshold (25 for clients, 5 for servers)?
If using subscription activation, is the device Azure AD joined (not just Azure AD registered/workplace joined)?
Has an Enterprise E3/E5 license recently been assigned to or removed from a user on this device?
Is the device's clock in sync, and is any VPN client such as Palo Alto GlobalProtect installed?
Does the environment use Active Directory-based Activation (ADBA), and if so, was the AD activation object published from a machine with the November 2018+ rollup installed?
If this is a Hyper-V guest VM, is Automatic Virtual Machine Activation (AVMA) in use, and is the Hyper-V host itself currently activated?
If this is subscription activation, which Azure AD account was used to join the device, and does it hold an active E3/E5 (or A3/A5 for education) license?
Does the problematic machine have any 3rd-party antivirus, security lockdown, or non-Microsoft disk encryption software installed?

l1: Run 'slmgr /xpr' to check current activation status.
Run 'slmgr /dlv' for detailed license information, including channel and partial product key.
Check Settings > System > Activation for the exact error text.
Run 'dsregcmd /status' to confirm Azure AD join state for subscription activation scenarios.
Run 'nslookup -type=srv _vlmcs._tcp' to confirm a KMS host record is published and visible from the client.
l2: On the KMS host, run 'cscript slmgr.vbs /dlv all > slmgr.txt' and search for 'Current Count' under each host key.
Check DNS SRV records with 'nslookup -type=all _vlmcs._tcp' to confirm KMS host discovery.
If subscription activation reverted to Pro, compare msinfo32 OS name and slmgr /dlv (which will correctly show Pro RETAIL by design) against dsregcmd /status.
Run 'w32tm /query /status' to check for clock drift if a time-mismatch error (0xC004F074/0xC004F06C) is reported.

For MAK activation counts, check with the Microsoft Activation Call Center — MAKs and KMS host keys both carry a hard activation limit (KMS host keys: 10 activations across up to 6 machines by default).
Run 'slmgr /ao-list' to confirm whether an Active Directory activation object is visible to this client.
Check the current Forest and Domain functional/schema level if AD-based activation objects are involved.
Run 'Test-NetConnection <KMS host> -Port 1688' (or telnet on port 1688) to confirm the client can actually reach the KMS host over the network, not just resolve it in DNS.

l1: Run 'slmgr /ato' to force an activation attempt.
Confirm network connectivity to the KMS host on TCP 1688.
Re-enter the correct product key if MAK-based activation is used.
Restart the Software Protection service (sppsvc) and retry.
Run the built-in Activation Troubleshooter from Settings > System > Activation > Troubleshoot before escalating.
Confirm the product key being used actually matches the installed edition (e.g. a Pro key won't activate an Enterprise install).
l2: KMS count below threshold (0xC004F038): force a subset of clients to point at the new host with 'slmgr /skms <host:1688>' then 'slmgr /ato', or use VAMT to bulk re-activate clients.
Time mismatch (0xC004F074 with 0xC004F06C): run 'w32tm /resync' as admin to resync against the DC or internet time source.
System/store tampered (0xC004D301, 0xC004D317) recurring: check for Palo Alto GlobalProtect VPN — uninstall or upgrade to 4.1.7+, a known trigger for false tamper detection.

Subscription activation stepping back down to Pro: confirm the user with the assigned E3/E5 license is still logging in; if intentionally staying on KMS, set HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\ClipSVC\Parameters\DisableSubscription to 1 to block automatic step-up.
0xC004F009 (MAK grace period expired): the system has entered the Notifications state — install a valid MAK or convert to KMS/subscription activation, then run 'slmgr /ato'.

0x8007232B / 0x8007007B (DNS name does not exist — KMS client cannot find the KMS SRV record): verify the _vlmcs._tcp SRV record exists in DNS, or point the client directly at a host with 'slmgr /skms <host>:1688'.
0xC004C020 (MAK exceeded its activation limit): contact the Microsoft Activation Call Center for a new MAK, or migrate the affected devices to KMS/Active Directory-based activation instead.

0xC004F050 (activation servers busy, or significant hardware change such as a motherboard swap): wait and retry, or run 'slmgr /upk' on the old installation before activating the same key on the replacement hardware.

If the KMS host's Current Count never rises above 1 despite enough clients, the deployed image was likely never generalized: run 'sysprep /generalize' (or KB929829's CMID reset workaround) so each client gets a unique Client Machine ID (CMID) instead of sharing one from the master image.

l1: Record the output of 'slmgr /xpr' and 'slmgr /dlv'.
Note the exact error code from Settings > Activation.
Confirm the product key type in use — KMS, MAK, AD-based, or subscription.
Note whether the device is domain-joined, Azure AD joined, or hybrid.
l2: Collect 'cscript slmgr.vbs /dlv all' output from both the client and the KMS host.
Collect 'dsregcmd /status' output (from a non-elevated prompt) for subscription-activation cases.
Capture a screenshot of Settings > Accounts > Access work or school and Settings > Activation.
If tamper-related, note any VPN client software (name and version) installed on the device.

activation_error_after_reimage.title: Device shows activation error after re-image

steps.action: Run 'slmgr /xpr'
steps.expect: Shows the current activation state and error, if any

steps.action: Run 'slmgr /dlv' to inspect license status and key channel
steps.expect: Confirms whether the wrong key channel is installed

steps.action: Install the correct KMS client key with 'slmgr /ipk'
steps.expect: Key installs without error

steps.action: Run 'slmgr /ato'
steps.expect: Activation succeeds and reports product activated

steps.action: Re-run 'slmgr /xpr'
steps.expect: Displays a valid, non-expiring activated status

subscription_activation_reverts_to_pro.title: Windows 10/11 Enterprise subscription activation reverts to Pro

steps.action: Check msinfo32 OS Name — if it shows Professional rather than Enterprise, the device has stepped down
steps.expect: Confirms the device reverted from Enterprise to Pro

steps.action: Confirm whether the user holding the E3/E5 license has logged off or had the license unassigned
steps.expect: Identifies the trigger for the step-down (this is expected behavior by design)

steps.action: Run 'dsregcmd /status' to confirm the device is Azure AD joined and not only Azure AD registered
steps.expect: Rules out an AADJ + workplace-join conflict as the cause

steps.action: Have the E3/E5-licensed user sign back in to re-trigger the automatic step-up to Enterprise
steps.expect: Device steps back up to Enterprise subscription activation

steps.action: If the environment intentionally uses KMS and wants to block automatic subscription step-up, set HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\ClipSVC\Parameters\DisableSubscription to 1, reboot, then reactivate via KMS with 'slmgr /ipk NPPR9-FWDCX-D2C8J-H872K-2YT43' and 'slmgr /ato'
steps.expect: Device stays on KMS-activated Enterprise without subscription interference

steps.action: Re-check Settings > Activation and msinfo32
steps.expect: Shows the intended edition (Enterprise) consistently

kms_count_below_threshold_0xc004f038.title: KMS clients fail with 0xC004F038 — count below minimum threshold

steps.action: On the KMS host, run 'cscript slmgr.vbs /dlv' and check 'Current Count'
steps.expect: Count is below 25 (clients) or 5 (servers)

steps.action: Confirm how many client machines have actually pointed at this host recently
steps.expect: Identifies whether it's a discovery problem or genuinely too few clients

steps.action: On several clients, run 'slmgr /skms <host FQDN or IP>:1688' then 'slmgr /ato' to force them to register against the host
steps.expect: Current Count on the host increases with each successful client activation

steps.action: Once past the threshold, run 'slmgr /ckms' on those clients to revert to automatic DNS-based discovery
steps.expect: Clients resume using standard DNS SRV discovery

steps.action: Re-check 'Current Count' on the host and retry activation on the originally failing client
steps.expect: Count is at or above threshold and the client activates successfully

dns_kms_record_missing_0x8007232b.title: KMS client fails with 0x8007232B / 0x8007007B — DNS SRV record not found

steps.action: Run 'nslookup -type=all _vlmcs._tcp' from the affected client
steps.expect: Confirms whether the KMS SRV record resolves in DNS

steps.action: Check the DNS zone for a manually published _vlmcs._tcp SRV record if auto-publishing from the KMS host is disabled
steps.expect: Identifies whether the record is missing, stale, or pointing at the wrong host

steps.action: Republish the SRV record from the KMS host with 'slmgr /cdns' then remove and re-add via 'net stop slsvc && net start slsvc' (or add it manually in DNS)
steps.expect: SRV record now resolves correctly

steps.action: As an interim fix, point the client directly at the host with 'slmgr /skms <host FQDN>:1688' then 'slmgr /ato'
steps.expect: Client activates successfully while DNS is corrected

steps.action: Run 'slmgr /xpr' on the client
steps.expect: Shows a valid, non-expiring activated status

kms_count_stuck_at_one_duplicate_cmid.title: KMS Current Count never rises above 1 — duplicate Client Machine IDs

steps.action: On the KMS host, run 'slmgr /dlv' repeatedly across several clients activating and confirm Current Count stays at 1
steps.expect: Count does not increase even though more clients are activating

steps.action: Check whether the deployed image was captured without running 'sysprep /generalize' first
steps.expect: Confirms client machines are sharing one Client Machine ID (CMID) from the master image

steps.action: Apply the CMID reset workaround from KB929829 on affected clients as an interim fix
steps.expect: Each client generates a unique CMID and registers separately with the KMS host

steps.action: Re-capture the reference image using 'sysprep /generalize /oobe /shutdown' before future deployments
steps.expect: New deployments each get a unique CMID from first boot

steps.action: Re-check 'slmgr /dlv' Current Count on the KMS host after several clients activate
steps.expect: Count rises correctly as new, uniquely-identified clients activate

activation_troubleshooter_walkthrough.title: Using the built-in Activation Troubleshooter for a straightforward first pass

steps.action: Open Settings > System > Activation and confirm an error/troubleshoot option is offered
steps.expect: Troubleshooter is available for this scenario

steps.action: Run the troubleshooter and note which specific issue it reports (e.g. hardware change, key mismatch, subscription lapse)
steps.expect: Troubleshooter narrows down the likely cause automatically

steps.action: Follow the troubleshooter's suggested remediation (e.g. sign in with the Microsoft account tied to the original license)
steps.expect: Guided fix resolves common straightforward cases without manual slmgr work

steps.action: Re-check Settings > Activation
steps.expect: Shows Windows is activated; escalate to manual slmgr-based playbooks only if this doesn't resolve it

generic_key_blocked_0xc004e016.title: Activation blocked with 0xC004E016 — generic/blocked key detected

steps.action: Run 'slmgr /dlv' and confirm the installed key is a generic/GVLK placeholder key rather than a real MAK/KMS key
steps.expect: Confirms a generic key is installed instead of the intended license key

steps.action: Confirm which real key (KMS client key, MAK, or retail) should be installed for this edition and channel
steps.expect: Identifies the correct key to install

steps.action: Install the correct key with 'slmgr /ipk <key>' then run 'slmgr /ato'
steps.expect: Activation succeeds with the correct key

steps.action: Run 'slmgr /xpr'
steps.expect: Shows a valid, non-expiring activated status
